events.reason: Low blood pressure during research study

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Received by fax 07/24/2026 from an outside hospital emergency department. Filed; reviewed by PCP.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN NOTE
Date of service: 07/16/2026
Arrival: brought over by staff of a university research study

HPI: 30 year old woman enrolled as a volunteer in a university study comparing how men and women regulate blood pressure. During a session this afternoon study staff recorded a blood pressure lower than their protocol allows and sent her here for evaluation. She feels fine. Denies lightheadedness, palpitations, or tiredness. No syncope, chest pain, or shortness of breath. Eating and drinking normally. Activity level ordinary for her age.

PMH: endometriosis.
Medications: ibuprofen 400 mg every 6 hours as needed for pelvic pain; naproxen sodium 220 mg every 8 hours as needed for menstrual cramps.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother with endometriosis; maternal aunt with infertility.

Exam: BMI 21. Alert, well appearing, in no distress. Mucous membranes moist. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Extremities warm, cap refill brisk. Neuro nonfocal.

Vitals: triage BP 88/56, HR 72, SpO2 99% RA, T 36.8, RR 14. Repeat BP 96/60, HR 72. At discharge BP 102/66, HR 72. Over serial checks her mean arterial pressure stayed toward the low end of normal, and the study team notes this is lower than in male participants of similar age and fitness.

Labs: electrolytes, renal function, and hemoglobin within normal limits.

Information from the research team (results not attached): her study screening showed normal renin, aldosterone and catecholamine levels; baroreceptor reflex testing preserved; sympathetic nerve activity normal; endothelium-dependent vasodilation enhanced on their testing.

MDM: Asymptomatic young woman with a transient low pressure reading in a research setting, normal labs, normal heart rate, improving pressures without intervention, and a normal study workup by report. No evidence of bleeding, infection, or volume loss.

Impression: hypotension, transient, resolved.
Disposition: discharged home in good condition. Fluids and regular meals; return for fainting, chest pain, or feeling unwell. Follow up with primary care.

documents.title: FYI ER visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! Quick update, I ended up in the ER a couple weeks ago, kind of a silly story. I volunteered for a blood pressure study on campus and my pressure read too low for their protocol so they made me go get checked. I felt totally normal the whole time. They said everything was fine. Is there anything I should do?

documents.title: RE: FYI ER visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know. I got their record last week and read it: your labs were normal, your pressure came up on its own, and you never had symptoms. Nothing you need to change. If you ever feel faint or lightheaded, tell me. Separately, it's been a while since I've seen you and your physical and Pap are overdue, so book something when your schedule allows.
